resources.string: Diagnostic build for capture feasibility. Translation and permanent history are not implemented. Nothing is uploaded. Consent resets when this process ends.
Cellular radio detected. Reception and complete-body extraction still need testing.
Wi-Fi-only hardware cannot receive cellular emergency alerts. Normal automatic capture is unavailable. Local injection experiments do not prove radio reception.
Cellular capability is inconsistent or unverified. Current Wi-Fi use, SIM absence, and mobile data settings do not determine hardware capability.
These package adapters are unverified. Other source packages need inspection before collection; this is not a manufacturer restriction or a universal support claim.
Allow local injection testing without verified cellular hardware
Accept only shell notifications tagged test_alert as explicit test fixtures
Changing capture consent or diagnostic options clears temporary observations and invalidates pending reads.

Withdraw session consent and clear observations

On affected Android 13+ APK installs, open App info → More → Allow restricted settings if offered. Then enable notification access or accessibility separately. Menu names may vary or be restricted by an administrator. Nothing is granted automatically; actual access is checked when you return.
Open Android Settings → Apps → CodeClear capture probe, then find the relevant access setting. This device did not allow the settings shortcut.

Only the latest 40 observations remain in memory. This diagnostic buffer is separate from future user history, which will remain until deletion. Leaving or restarting the process can lose these observations.
No observations. This does not prove that no emergency alert was issued or received.

Android notification access can expose notifications from other apps. This probe filters to installed system emergency-receiver package candidates before reading text, plus shell test_alert fixtures only when you enable that option. It holds titles and bodies only in a bounded in-memory buffer for inspection. No network upload, saved file, translation, or automatic screen opening. You can withdraw consent here or revoke access in system settings. Consent ends with this process. Agree only if you want to test this route.

This probe uses accessibility to inspect only the two declared system emergency-receiver package candidates. It reads the message resource field in the active matching window, with bounded traversal. It does not read arbitrary screens, perform gestures, dismiss alerts, or bypass protected content. Text stays only in a bounded in-memory inspection buffer; nothing is uploaded. This is not a disability accessibility tool. Withdraw consent here or revoke system access at any time. Consent ends with this process.

Enable diagnostic collection for supported local injection experiments even when radio hardware is absent or unknown. This does not enable cellular reception or guarantee that a production firmware accepts injected messages. It is available only in this diagnostic build.
OS notification post time: %1$s (not disaster occurrence time)
Completeness unverified. Compare every character with the known original; visible text alone is not proof of full capture.
Extraction limit or multiple body fields encountered. Treat this as incomplete or ambiguous.

This body matches a known Android notification text-length boundary. The original may have been shortened before reaching this app. Compare it with the system alert; this warning does not prove that text is missing.
Group summary: do not treat this as an individual alert body.
No readable body field exposed. No text has been reconstructed.
